citation: Jalleh RJ, Marathe CS, Trahair LG, et al. A Biphasic Glucose Response during an Oral Glucose Tolerance Test Is Associated with Greater Plasma Insulin and GLP-1 Responses and a Reduction in 1-Hour Glucose but Does Not Relate to the Rate of Gastric Emptying in Healthy, Older Adults. Nutrients. 2023.
protocol: 75 g glucose drink (with 150 mg 13C-acetate) after overnight fast (14 h solids, 12 h liquids), 08:30; samples at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 min; initial study and follow-up (~6 y later) with identical protocol
population: n=36 older adults without diabetes (22 monophasic, 14 biphasic glucose response); age 77.3+/-0.7 and 69.2+/-0.9 y (mean+/-SEM); BMI ~25.6-26.0

reports.where: Table 2 (initial) and Table 3 (follow-up): fasting, 1 h, 2 h, peak, AUC

note: Older-adult flag. Reported by curve-shape group (monophasic vs biphasic), not pooled. Insulin is labelled pmol/L but the values (fasting ~4) look like mU/L; check units before use. Gastric emptying by breath test also measured.
